newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse lifted by new gains.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse lifted by new gains.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 1.57 percent higher, boosted by steel mill Sonasid, Wafabank, edible oil firm Lesieur and privatisation bonds, a broker said.
The all-share index closed at 595.88 from 586.68 points on Wednesday.
"The index was lifted by gains in these companies and new interest for privatisation bonds ahead of the possible privatisation of Imiter silver mine," a broker at Wafa Bourse stockbrokers said.
Steel mill Sonasid took 30 dirhams to 532 dirhams.
In the banking sector, one of the best performers was Wafabank which jumped 24 dirhams to 795 dirhams.
"The banking sector is losing ground but Wafabank is still going up with people anticipating result of its merger with Spanish bank Uniban in terms of a larger network," a broker at Wafa Bourse said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur fell seven dirhams from Wednesday's close to trade at 570 dirhams with only 35 shares exchanged on the official market.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest private bank, slipped five dirhams to 845 dirhams with 2,710 shares traded.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique fell six dirhams to 215 dirhams. Some 26,487 shares changed hands on the official market.
Mortgage Bank Credit Immobilier et Hotelier was up nine dirhams to 315 dirhams with 950 shares traded.
Morocco's main oil refinery Samir rose one dirham to 281 with 18,408 shares traded.
The refinery said on Wednesday it had posted a net profit of 506.7 million dirhams ($54.5 million) in 1996 from 423.3 million dirhams in 1995.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, advanced to 717 dirhams, up seven dirhams.
The company published on Thursday provisional results
